prologue: Veydal. A valley of lakes and terraces, drawn and redrawn by its cartographers.
Last night a storm tore the sky open above the lake.
Where the lightning struck, Rifts opened, and the Spirlings near them fell silent.
In the Brindlewick lighthouse, an apprentice cartographer is still asleep...

lines: Pinned under the mossy rock: a sheet of old paper!
Something flutters in a crack in the rock. Paper!
A torn page is caught in the fence.
A page drifts by the bank. The ink is still readable.
Deep in the gallery, a page lies dry under a ledge.

page_1: 'Day one. The sky over the lake split like old paper. I'm going in to map it.'
'Aldo says I'm mad. Aldo is usually right.'
page_2: 'The ferns all lean toward the Rift, as if they were listening.'
'The Spirlings here have stopped calling. I'll name it the Hush.'
page_3: 'A Warden holds a Rift shut only while their bond holds.'
'A bond is a promise heard on both sides. Break it, and the Hush gets in.'
page_4: 'Inside, the land isn't broken. It's unfinished, like a map nobody drew to the edge.'
page_5: 'Something on the other side answers when I call.'
'Not a voice. An echo of every Spirling that ever lost its Wayfarer.'
page_6: 'If I don't come back: a Rift closes when someone draws it to the end.'
'Tell Aldo to keep the lamp lit. Light finds the way home.'

lines: Behind a loose board under the lamp stairs: a folded letter.
'Aldo. If you find this, you finally fixed the stairs. I knew you would. M.'
Under the rock, wrapped in oilcloth: a letter in Mirela's hand.
'The ferns talk when the wind is right. You'd laugh. I miss your laugh. M.'
A small tin floats in the pond, tied to a reed. A letter inside!
'If I'm late, keep my side of the bed cold. I hate warm sheets. M.'
That's all three of Mirela's letters from Veydal. Aldo should read them.

page_7: 'Day forty? Day four hundred? Time runs slow in here. The ink dries before I lift the pen.'
page_8: 'Paths here only exist once I draw them. I drew a path to a lake, and the lake came.'
page_9: 'Every Spirling is born here, at the edge of drawing.'
'They wander out through the thin places, and the first person they meet becomes their world.'
page_10: 'At the heart of this land there is a voice made of many voices.'
'It grieves. It is not angry. It is lonely.'
page_11: 'I call it the Echo. Every bond that breaks adds one more voice.'
'When it is loud, it leaks out through the Rifts. That is the Hush.'
page_12: 'The Wide Rift tears wider every year. When I draw its edge from in here, it holds.'
page_13: 'So I stay. A Warden from the far side.'
'Aldo, keep the lamp lit. Some nights I can see it from here.'
page_14: 'The Echo does not want a fight. It wants an answer.'
'Someone has to sing back. I am too old to sing it alone.'

lines: Tucked between two mooring posts: a page with a compass rose in the corner!
A page lies flat on the still water, as if someone set it down gently.
Caught in the woad stems, stained blue: one of Mirela's pages!
Weighed down with a grey stone on the ridge: a page from the map book.
In the ash by the station platform: a page, edges singed but readable.
Wedged in the kiln wall, warm to the touch: another page!
Under a sheet of salt glass, sealed like a pressed flower: a page.
Pinned to the gravers' notice board, as if waiting for you: the last page.
A letter, scorched at one corner, lies under a cairn at the edge.
'Aldo. The Rift is wider than I thought. Do not come after me. I mean it. M.'
Folded into a dye pot's lid: an old letter in Mirela's hand.
'The dyers here taught me blue. I'll paint the lighthouse door when I'm home. M.'
In a tin box under the boardwalk: a letter, dry and folded small.
'The moor is so quiet. I hum to it. Our song. It hums back, I swear. M.'
Three letters from Corvane. Pim at the guild house will want to read them.
